source_claim: tasks define the program artifact and evaluator interface, and AlphaEvolve can operate on existing codebases and task-specific program representations rather than only one Python-primary workspace shape
claim_boundary: This boundary records that LibreEvolve has a validated task-primary candidate-language policy, stage-bound local build and runner commands, problem-owned scoring, bounded generated-artifact capture, and an executed non-Python expression fixture, one checked host C compiler fixture with toolchain/lock identity, and optional exact-pin enforcement. It also records one digest-pinned OCI Python fixture contract with immutable image identity, optional pull-if-missing, network-disabled read-only-rootfs candidate build/run processes, bounded resources, ordered in-image toolchain probes, and values-redacted runtime connectivity metadata. The live OCI integration test remains opt-in and is not a committed cross-host certification. This does not claim AlphaEvolve-style arbitrary language or build-system parity with language-aware marker grammars, hostile-code sandboxing, broad package-manager provisioning, deterministic cross-platform replay, task-defined abstraction hooks, arbitrary-runner environment artifacts, or codebase-scale generated build-artifact evidence.
